subject: Intermittent streaming lag — bridging steps, short-term mitigations, and post-incident checklist
content:
From: Emma Turner <emma.turner@novaweb.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected lag in live chat streams (multiple regions)

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing intermittent stalls in our web chat this morning around 08:45 PT. Tokens are arriving in bursts; sometimes messages take 6–8s between chunks (normally <300ms). This has affected our agent UI and a handful of active users. We've attached session snippets and a short network capture. Can your team confirm if there's an ongoing issue and share any immediate mitigations?

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Turner
Head of Support — NovaWeb

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 09:34:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected lag in live chat streams (multiple regions)

Hi Emma — thanks for the quick report and the logs. We see a subset of your streams hitting higher per-token latency in our US-West edge pool between 08:30–09:10 PT.

Short-term actions we've applied:
- Throttled routing for affected sessions to the lower-concurrency warm pool (reduces queueing).
- Enabled prefix KV cache for your account for active sessions to avoid re-computation.
- Instrumented additional telemetry (you may see expanded trace IDs in the attachments).

Please try reconnecting a test agent session now and let me know if you still observe the 6–8s gaps. If it looks better we'll keep the bridge in place while we continue investigation.

Attachment: streaming-debug-log-1018.txt (text)

Best,
Marissa Cole

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Oct 2028 10:02:50 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected lag in live chat streams (multiple regions)

Marissa — quick notes from infra triage:
- Root cause signal points to an inefficient kernel selection path for a particular quantized variant when sequence lengths spike (customer sequences with many short messages). This causes CPU fallback on a minority of requests that then impacts streaming inter-token cadence.
- Impacted nodes were concentrated in a single US-West shard; autoscaler did not spin up additional warm instances fast enough because the spike coincided with a slow health-checking window (edge health probe delay).

Short-term mitigation proposed (we can do immediately):
1) Temporarily pin NovaWeb traffic to the nearby dedicated warm pool (reduces kernel variety and avoids the slow selection path).
2) Apply a transient conservative max_tokens and reduce streaming window to smaller chunks for affected sessions (client-side knob).
3) Enable a fallback non-streaming mode for sessions that experience >3s gap, with server-side buffering to deliver combined chunk as one message (keeps UX acceptable while we heal).

I'll coordinate the pool pin and can push the transient config. Need Marissa to confirm approval to apply steps 1 & 2 on your behalf.

-ben

Emma — thanks, quick update and proposed temporary configs (low risk):
- We'll pin your traffic to a nearby warm pool for the next 6 hours (we'll monitor closely and roll back once stable).
- Server-side: we will enable a buffered fallback for any session that has a token gap >3s. That means the UI will receive a single combined chunk rather than seeing prolonged gaps.
- Client-recommended optional change (you can opt in): set streaming_chunk_token_limit to 12 and max_response_tokens to 256 for high-concurrency agent sessions. This reduces the kernel-selection variance.

If you approve, we'll apply the pin and server fallback immediately (we expect visible improvement within 5–7 minutes).

Best,
Marissa

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: Emma Turner <emma.turner@novaweb.com>, Support Team <support@novaweb.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Oct 2028 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: streaming token gaps on 2028-10-18 (summary & recommended actions)

Emma / NovaWeb team — thanks again for your patience while we investigated. Below is a concise post-incident follow-up and recommended actions (we've kept the language non-technical for ops readers and included a short checklist).

Incident summary:
- Window: 2028-10-18 08:30–09:10 PT.
- Symptom: intermittently elevated inter-token latency in streaming chat (6–8s gaps on affected sessions).
- Root cause (short): an inefficient kernel-selection path triggered by spikes in short message sequences combined with delayed autoscaler health checks in a US-West edge shard.

Immediate mitigations applied (10:40–10:45 PT):
- Pinned NovaWeb traffic to a nearby warm pool to reduce kernel variety.
- Enabled server-side buffered fallback for sessions exceeding 3s inter-token gaps.
- Applied transient conservative streaming_chunk_token_limit and max_response_tokens settings for high-concurrency agent sessions (optional for client; we recommend canarying).

Observed outcome:
- >2s gaps reduced from ~7% to ~0.8% of active sessions within 10 minutes of actions.
- No data exposure or retention changes. No customer data was processed differently.

Recommended client actions (short checklist):
- Canary the client-side knob: streaming_chunk_token_limit = 12, max_response_tokens = 256 for 5–10% of agent traffic for 24 hours.
- Add a 3s local debounce to your UI that temporarily hides partial streaming gaps (improves perceived UX when server fallback combines chunks).
- If you have session-level retries, set a 7s threshold to trigger non-stream fallback.

Planned platform fixes & timeline (for transparency):
- Short-term (this week): autoscaler health-check timing fix (deployed) and additional warm-pool capacity for US-West (in progress).
- Medium-term (2–4 weeks): kernel-selection optimization for quantized variants and improved early-detection telemetry.
- Long-term: model-variant scheduling overhaul to reduce cross-variant variance during small-sequence workloads.

Attachments: novaweb-ops-snapshot-1018.pdf, runbook-short-term-mitigations.md

If you'd like a short 20-minute sync to walk through the checklist and confirm canary settings, I'm available Monday morning PT. Otherwise we'll keep the transient pin in place for 24 hours and then evaluate whether to keep it for a longer scheduled maintenance window while we deploy the variant fix.

Best regards,
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
